definition: the group of people watching or listening to an event or contest.
example: The audience cheered loudly at the end of the final round.

definition: the person or team that wins a competition.
example: She was declared the champion after three flawless performances.
spellingTip: The middle sounds like pee, but it is spelt p-i-o.

definition: a formal event held for a special occasion such as prize-giving.
example: The medal ceremony began just after the last race.

definition: a person who takes part in a competition.
example: Each contestant had one minute to answer the question.
originNote: from a root meaning to strive
spellingTip: The ending is -ant, like in assistant.

definition: a choice or judgement made after considering options.
example: The judge's decision ended the debate instantly.
originNote: from a root meaning cut off
spellingTip: The ending is -sion, sounding like zhuhn.

definition: a person or team competing against another.
example: Her opponent was calm but very determined.
originNote: from a root meaning set against
spellingTip: Double the p in the middle: op-po-nent.

definition: an official who enforces the rules in a match.
example: The referee stopped play to explain the penalty.
originNote: from a word meaning refer back
spellingTip: It ends with double e, not just one.

definition: a person who watches an event or competition.
example: Every spectator stood to applaud the winning team.
spellingTip: Remember spect- like inspect and spectacle.

definition: a series of contests to decide an overall winner.
example: Our school hosted a chess tournament on Saturday.
spellingTip: The first part is tour-, not torn-.

definition: a great victory or success in a contest.
example: The final goal was a triumph for the underdogs.
originNote: from a word for victory celebration
spellingTip: The ph says f at the end.

definition: having won a contest or competition.
example: The victorious team waved to the crowd.
spellingTip: Keep the base word victory in mind.

definition: a person trained in sports and physical contests.
example: Each athlete waited quietly before the relay began.
spellingTip: Do not forget the h after the a.

definition: allowed to take part according to the rules.
example: Only Year 8 students were eligible for the final heat.
originNote: from a root meaning choose out

definition: to lose the right to continue because of a rule breach.
example: The team had to forfeit the match after arriving too late.
originNote: from a word meaning do wrong
spellingTip: The ending is -feit, which sounds like fit.

definition: to meet the conditions needed to enter or continue.
example: Two runners will qualify for the state final.
originNote: from a root meaning of what kind
spellingTip: It starts with qua-, not kwa-.

definition: a careful plan for winning a game or contest.
example: Their strategy changed after the first round.
originNote: from a root meaning army leadership
spellingTip: The middle sounds like j but is spelt g.

definition: a prize awarded to the winner of a competition.
example: The captain lifted the trophy above her head.
originNote: from a root meaning turning point of victory
spellingTip: The ph makes an f sound.

definition: an official who applies the rules in some sports.
example: The umpire signalled the player was out.
originNote: from a word meaning non-peer judge
spellingTip: It begins with um-, not un-.
